news.title: Full year 2026 earnings: EPS and revenues miss analyst expectations
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹2.21 (down from ₹2.72 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹30.7b (up 89% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹809.2m (down 6.9% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 2.6% (down from 5.4% in FY 2025). Revenue missed analyst estimates by 4.6%. Earnings per share (EPS) also missed analyst estimates by 13%. Revenue is expected to decline by 2.0% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, while revenues in the Entertainment industry in Asia are expected to grow by 8.4%. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 2% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 22% per year, which means it is tracking significantly ahead of earnings growth.

news.title: New major risk - Revenue and earnings growth
news.body: Earnings are forecast to decline by an average of 83% per year for the foreseeable future. This is considered a major risk. Ultimately, shareholders want to see a good return on their investment and that generally comes from sharing in the company's profits. If profits are expected to decline, then in most cases the share price will decline over time as well. In addition, if the company pays dividends it will also likely need to reduce or cut them, striking a dual blow to total shareholder returns. This is currently the only risk that has been identified for the company.

news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings: EPS and revenues miss analyst expectations
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹0.29 (down from ₹0.96 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹4.06b (down 24% from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹109.3m (down 64% from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 2.7% (down from 5.7% in 3Q 2025). The decrease in margin was driven by lower revenue. Revenue missed analyst estimates by 14%. Earnings per share (EPS) also missed analyst estimates by 58%. Revenue is forecast to grow 12% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 11% growth forecast for the Entertainment industry in Asia. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 82% per year but the company’s share price has only increased by 26% per year, which means it is significantly lagging earnings growth.
